findings.title: UUID v1/v6 random node ID lacks multicast bit, can collide with real MACs
findings.description:
Entry: node.go:39 (setNodeInterface), reached from NewUUID (version1.go:38), NewV6 (version6.go:77) and NodeID() (node.go:64) when no interface has a usable hardware address.
Attacker: any workload or host that generates UUIDs while owning no usable hardware address; it writes a random value into the IEEE MAC namespace it does not own, crossing the boundary between randomly assigned node values and real hardware addresses.
Path: getHardwareInterface returns "", nil (node_net.go:32), so setNodeInterface takes the fallback branch and calls randomBits(nodeID[:]) (node.go:52), filling nodeID with 48 random bits; version1.go:40 and version6.go:79 then copy those bits into the node field of every generated UUID with no marker that they are random.
Why nothing stops it: randomBits only fills bytes, and no code sets the multicast bit (the least significant bit of nodeID[0]) that RFC 4122 section 4.1.6 / RFC 9562 section 6.10 require for a randomly generated node, so the generated node is indistinguishable from a genuine MAC address and can collide with one.
Impact for this library: the node field of a UUID produced without a hardware address can equal a real device's MAC, so two different hosts can mint the same v1/v6 UUID whenever their timestamps and 14-bit clock sequences coincide, and consumers cannot tell a random node from a hardware-derived one, defeating the uniqueness/integrity guarantee the multicast-bit rule exists to protect.
Fix: after randomBits(nodeID[:]) set the multicast bit, e.g. nodeID[0] |= 0x01, and do the same wherever a random node value is installed, so a generated node is always a random multicast address and can never collide with a real MAC.

findings.title: Unsynchronized getTime call in NewV6WithTime yields duplicate v6 UUIDs
findings.description: NewV6WithTime (version6.go:39-45) calls getTime() without holding timeMu, while GetTime, ClockSequence, SetClockSequence, and getV7Time all lock it. This data race on clockSeq/lasttime can produce duplicate v6 UUIDs.
